Rebuttal:
It is a fact that solar activity follows a cycle of about 11 years of minima and maxima. The last maximum took place in 2001, and the next maximum is expected not on 21 December 2012 but in May 2013. During the maxima of solar activity there are more sunspots, flares and coronal mass ejections. Because of these phenomena huge amounts of energy are released, and particles are thrown out that often reach the Earth. But our planet, thanks to its magnetic field (the magnetosphere), is protected to a great extent. So however strong these phenomena are, they are no threat to life and certainly cannot cause natural disasters. The only danger concerns electronic systems, mainly those of satellites, or sometimes telecommunications, which may be damaged. In rarer cases power grids may also be affected, resulting in temporary power cuts.

This is impossible. It is known that the Earth's axis is not perpendicular to the plane of its orbit around the Sun but is tilted by about 23.5 degrees. <strong>Αντιστροφή των μαγνητικών πόλων:

Rebuttal:
First of all, we must distinguish the geographical from the magnetic poles. The geographical poles are particular areas at the northernmost and southernmost points of the Earth. The magnetic poles are what compass needles point towards. Because the Earth's magnetic field is created by processes that take place inside it, the magnetic poles do not correspond to fixed areas on the Earth's crust but move over time. For thousands of years the magnetic north pole, although it does not coincide with the geographical north pole, has been close enough to it that when a compass needle points we can safely assume that its direction also shows geographical north.
The magnetic poles move at such a speed that their positions are reversed about every 400,000 years. So we can see that this is not an event that can happen within a few hours or days, so that we could speak of a sudden reversal of the magnetic poles on a particular date. And a reversal of the magnetic poles has no reason to cause any disaster on Earth, except perhaps the need to readjust compasses.

Rebuttal:
First of all, “Nibiru” is another name for the ancient Eastern god Marduk. Specialists in Sumerian civilisation say that this name does not refer to a new planet discovered by the Sumerians (who in fact did not know of the existence of other – real – planets such as Uranus, Neptune and Pluto), but is another name for the planet Jupiter.
An attempt to support this scenario was made when in 1983 a NASA survey found sources of infrared radiation in the outer part of our solar system, which could point to the existence of a new planet. But studies published in the following years proved that the sources of infrared radiation were some distant galaxies and a nebula, and that there is in fact no new planet.
Finally, if a planet really were coming so close to the Earth that there was a risk of collision, this would have been noticed years ago, and as 21 December 2012 approached it would be visible even to the naked eye as the brightest object in the sky. Here, of course, the supporters of this theory claim that for some reason the planet Nibiru is invisible. But again this does not stand, because even if it were invisible, as it approached it would noticeably affect the orbits of the other planets through gravitational interactions, which would also be felt on Earth.
A new claim by the champions of this theory replies that NASA has observed this planet but is keeping it secret so as not to cause panic. But this claim does not stand either, since about 10,000 professional and 100,000 amateur astronomers around the world observe the night sky every day. Moreover, the largest telescopes in the world are not controlled by NASA, but are run by universities and academic institutions that simply supply NASA with the data from their observations. So it would be impossible for such an imminent worldwide danger to have been kept a closely guarded secret.

Αν θεωρήσουμε δύο ανθρώπους, ο ένας από: If we take two people, one moving and the other at rest, then for the one who is moving, time passes more slowly. How much more slowly? The greater his speed relative to the person at rest, the slower it passes. Indeed, for this effect to be large enough to be easily observed, the moving person's speed must be very high, close to the speed of light. But we should note here that these people do not notice the time lag, because when each looks at his own watch, time seems to flow normally. In reality, though, one second for the moving person corresponds to more than one second for the person at rest (for a better understanding of the effect, please see the related articles in the right-hand column). The rate at which time flows is also affected by the gravitational field we are in. The greater the mass of a body (and so the stronger its gravitational field), the greater the time lag. So on the surface of a planet with a much greater mass than the Earth's, time flows more slowly, and a 24-hour day on that planet may correspond to many Earth years. Indeed, right at the event horizon of a black hole, whose gravitational field is so strong that not even light can escape, time almost stops.

The theory of abiogenesis, or spontaneous generation, is the cornerstone of the theory of evolution. According to this theory, living matter can arise from non-living chemical components. Although Darwin himself did not deal with abiogenesis but with the evolution of living organisms from the level of the cell upwards, the spontaneous generation of life is a necessary condition for the theory of evolution to stand, because it tries to explain how the cell, the basic structural and functional unit of life, came into existence, so that evolution could then take place.

Ideas about the spontaneous generation of life already existed in ancient times, while the term “abiogenesis” became established in the 19th century and expressed people's belief that new living organisms can arise from dead matter as it decomposes. The many examples from everyday life, such as maggots appearing in rotting meat, were enough to count as unshakeable proof of the spontaneous generation of life.

But in 1861 the theory of abiogenesis was finally overturned by Louis Pasteur, whose experiments proved that the microbes and insects seen on spoiled meat are not born spontaneously from dead matter, but come from eggs laid on the meat earlier by insects or micro-organisms. So the principle of biogenesis was stated: “omne vivum ex vivo”, that is, all life comes from life.

To deal with the problem of how the first living cell came about, the Russian biochemist Alexander Oparin proposed in 1924 that life arose by chance from chemical reactions in the warm primitive oceans, given that the atmosphere must have been rich in ammonia, methane and hydrogen. Sources of energy, such as heat from volcanoes and lightning, acted on carbon compounds, turning them into more complex ones.

In an attempt to verify this theory, in 1953 Stanley Miller carried out a series of experiments using the components that he believed reproduced the conditions of the early Earth where life might have appeared (the primordial soup). In suitable laboratory chambers (vessels) he placed water, methane and ammonia. He boiled the mixture and exposed it to an electric discharge. After a week some amino acids were found in the mixture. This caused great excitement at how easily the amino acids that make up proteins – the building blocks of cells – could be produced. But the excitement soon faded, because from this mixture of “bare” amino acids it was impossible by any means to go on to form a protein, and so none of the other more complex molecules that make up living matter.

Newer scientific evidence has shown that Miller's experiment, and any other similar experiment, could in no way prove that a living cell can be put together from non-living components. Besides, the conditions of that experiment were chosen in order to get the desired result, and not on the basis of estimates of the real conditions on the early Earth.

Man's highest means of communication, unlike the animals', is speech. In the same way Holy Scripture, which is the Word of God, speaks directly into the heart, the spirit, the mind and the conscience of the sincere person.

Holy Scripture was written over a period of about 15 centuries by about 40 different writers. It is made up of the Old Testament and the New Testament, and it makes a very serious claim: “It is the Word of God”.

This claim proves itself when a sincere person takes Holy Scripture into their hands. Even so, we want to look at the reliability of Holy Scripture not only as the result of its effect on a person's life, which is the primary evidence of its reliability (1 Thess. 2:13), but also through archaeology and the study of ancient texts.

The writers of Holy Scripture are about 40 different people who lived in different eras and different social and political settings. Yet the result is a unified book: reading Holy Scripture, you do not feel that you are moving from one book to another, but that it is the same book throughout.

This refutes the claim that the texts of Holy Scripture were an attempt by priesthoods and various centres of power to steer and control ordinary people, especially since, from time to time, it was the priesthoods of the day that persecuted those who believed and followed these texts.

In our coming topics we will look in more detail at the finds and conclusions of the famous scholar and archaeologist Sir W. Ramsay , who took up archaeology with the sole aim of proving that the account in the book of the Acts of the Apostles was wrong; yet after 25 years of research he proved the opposite and turned from atheism to Christianity.

A basic question is: how do we know that the text we read in the Old Testament today is the same as the original Hebrew text? First of all, as far as the text is concerned, there is the Septuagint translation into Greek, made in the 3rd century BC, and the Masoretic text, whose most recent manuscripts date from the 9th century AD, which is why their reliability was questioned. But in 1947 the Qumran manuscripts (the Dead Sea Scrolls) came to light; they date from the 2nd and 1st centuries BC, and they confirm the reliability of the Masoretic text.

An important factor that ensures that the Old Testament texts we hold today are faithful to the originals is that the copying of the manuscripts was entrusted to specialist copyists called Talmudists, who kept truly strict rules when copying the sacred texts, so as to avoid any error.

The differences between Holy Scripture, and especially the Old Testament, and the mythological accounts of ancient peoples are also obvious. The texts of Holy Scripture give a clear placing of events in space and time, complete consistency with historical and scientific facts, and impartiality in describing people: the people of Holy Scripture are not idealised; often their weaknesses are shown too. The clear purpose of all the texts is to exalt one person alone, Jesus Christ.

To confirm the above, we can, for example, compare the texts of Genesis about the Creation with the corresponding creation accounts of other ancient peoples, and above all with the Babylonian epic Enuma Elish. The superiority and distinctiveness of Genesis lie in the simplicity and consistency of its description, and in the uniqueness of its idea of creation out of nothing by a God who is outside space and time, and who is exactly one God, not many. This overturns the claim that the biblical account came from other ancient accounts, since the observed development of religion in human civilisation runs from monotheism to polytheism and never the other way round, and this is where we see the biblical account stand apart.

• Η αρχαιολογία άρχισε να εξελίσσεται κα: • Archaeology began to develop, and at some point the question arose whether there would be finds confirming the biblical accounts.
• Η αρχαιολογία είναι επιστήμη και δεν κ: • Archaeology is a science and does not accept evidence that “forces” Holy Scripture to be proved true. It rests on real and fully verified evidence.
• Η αρχαιολογία ξεκίνησε πριν από 150 χρ: • Archaeology began 150 years ago with people who believed that the ancient texts contain truths and tried to confirm it.
